Peripatetic

per-ih-puh-TET-ik · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Peripatetic is traveling from place to place, especially for work; itinerant.

As a peripatetic session musician, she spent more nights in tour buses and hotel rooms than in her own apartment.

Worked Example

The peripatetic diplomat crisscrossed three continents in a single month, negotiating trade deals in one capital before flying to the next.

Peripatetic describes a lifestyle or job built around constant movement -- not a single trip, but an ongoing pattern of traveling from place to place.

How Peripatetic Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

itinerant

itinerant: traveling from place to place for work (a word you met earlier in this course)

nomadic

nomadic: having no fixed home, moving from place to place

Antonyms

sedentary

sedentary: staying in one place, especially seated (a word you met earlier in this course)

stationary

stationary: not moving, fixed in place

How Strong Is It? — well-traveled → peripatetic → vagabond

well-traveled vs. peripatetic

well-traveled vs. peripatetic: Well-traveled describes someone who has traveled a fair amount, without necessarily being constantly on the move like a peripatetic worker.

vagabond vs. peripatetic

vagabond vs. peripatetic: A vagabond wanders with no fixed home at all, even more unmoored than someone merely peripatetic.

Build the Word

The pieces

prefix — peri-

prefix — peri-: around (Greek)

root — -patetic

root — -patetic: walking (Greek patein, 'to walk')

Put it together

Put it together: Peripatetic comes from Greek peri- ('around') + patein ('to walk') -- literally 'walking around.' Aristotle supposedly taught his students while walking around the school grounds, so his followers became known as the Peripatetic school of philosophy.

Use the root in a new word: peripheral

Use the root in a new word: peripheral: The coach kept an eye on the peripheral players warming up along the sideline -- peripheral shares the same peri- ('around') that starts peripatetic.
